a: A widely used list of critical web application security risks.
Users can act outside their permissions — always enforce authorization server-side.
Weak or missing encryption for sensitive data at rest or in transit.
Untrusted input interpreted as code/query — use parameterization and encoding.
Missing security controls in architecture and threat modeling.
Defaults, open ports, verbose errors, and unused features left enabled.
Outdated libraries with known CVEs — scan and patch dependencies.
Weak passwords, missing MFA, session issues, credential stuffing gaps.
Unsigned updates, insecure CI/CD, and untrusted deserialization.
Missing logs and alerts delay detection of attacks.
